q: Temam's notion of the universal attractor for the Navier-Stokes equations has finite fractal dimension d_f (Mandelbrot). The physical interpretation is that:
opts: The flow has only d_f degrees of freedom for all time
Asymptotically, the flow is effectively finite-dimensional: only d_f modes are active on the attractor
The flow is always laminar for d_f < 3
exp: Finite fractal dimension of the attractor means turbulent flow has finite effective degrees of freedom (the number of active modes on the attractor). This justifies dimensional reduction and the use of finite-dimensional models (like reduced-order models) for turbulence.
